findings.title: Existing admin permissions client is not migrated when Clients scopes/resource are added
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. This PR adds a new Clients resource type and new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite), but realms that already have the admin permissions client will not get the new scopes or the 'Clients' all-resource created. Subsequent client-permission creation/evaluation can fail or silently deny, e.g. getOrCreateResource throws ModelException when a required scope is missing. An update/migration path is needed for existing realms.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when all-clients resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately passes the result to PolicyStore.findByResource. getResourceTypeResource can return null if the authorization schema is not supported for the realm/resource server. In that case this method throws NullPointerException instead of returning false. A null check is needed before using the resource.

findings.title: Individual authorization resources are created without persisting their resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates individual user/client resources with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission then searches with resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). If individual client resources do not have the type persisted, they will not be found by this query, so clients with individual permissions can be omitted from permission-based filtering, and only type-level resources may be processed. The resource type should be set when creating the resource.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve names for Client resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases only the Users resource type. For Client resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but client resources created by getOrCreateResource are stored with the client's internal ID as the name and no display name. As a result, permission representations/UI can show null or an internal ID instead of a useful client identifier. A Clients branch should resolve the client and return something meaningful such as client_id.

findings.title: Provider-event cleanup is gated on V1 feature and can break or skip cleanup under V2
findings.body: The listener now only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. However AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled, removal events will call setPermissionsEnabled on ClientPermissionsV2, which throws UnsupportedOperationException. If only V2 is enabled, removed clients can leave orphan FGAP authorization resources because no V2 cleanup is performed. The listener should either explicitly exclude V2 and provide V2-specific cleanup/no-op behavior.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission evaluates every client resource individually
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission iterates over all resources of type Clients and calls root.evaluatePermission for each one. In realms with many clients this becomes an N+1-style authorization evaluation and may make client listing/permission filtering expensive. A batched or cached evaluation strategy may be needed for large realms.

findings.title: No test coverage for the new map-roles-client-scope client permission
findings.body: The PR adds the map-roles-client-scope scope and ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles, but the new client permission tests only exercise MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. There is no integration test verifying that MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE allows or denies mapping client roles through client scopes, leaving the newly added scope unverified.
